key_insight: A 3D opto-electro-thermal COMSOL model shows that a n-ZnSe/p-SrScCu3Se4/p+-WSe2 heterostructure can achieve high photovoltaic efficiency when absorber width, doping, and defect levels are optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a realistic device-design framework for chalcogenide solar cells by linking geometry, materials properties, and thermal effects to performance metrics.
method: Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and thermal loss
Parameter sweep of absorber width, acceptor concentration, and bulk defects
evidence_signal: Under optimized conditions, the device reaches VOC 1.02 V, JSC 32.472 mA/cm2, FF 88.212%, and PCE 29.217%, with QE strongest in the visible range.
watch_item: Performance is simulation-based, so real-device outcomes may differ due to interface quality, fabrication defects, and thermal management limits.
paper_title: Computational analysis and performance optimization of SrScCu3Se4-based solar cells using COMSOL Multiphysics
